description_full: Genpact Limited, an agentic and advanced technology solutions company, provides digital transformation, business process management, technology, data, analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI) services to enterprises in India, the rest of Asia, North and Latin America, and Europe. Its Financial Services segment offers customer onboarding, customer service, collections, retail and commercial loan operations, payment operations, mortgage origination and servicing, compliance, wealth management, capital market operations support, financial crime and risk management, proprietary insurance policy suite, underwriting support, new business processing, policy administration, customer, claims management, catastrophe and exposure/risk modeling, actuarial services, end-to-end third-party administration for property and casualty claims, and technology services. The company's Consumer and Healthcare segment provides demand generation, sensing and planning, supply chain planning and management, pricing and trade promotion management, deduction recovery management, order management, digital commerce, customer experience, lifecycle management, regulatory operations, chemistry manufacturing control compliance, regulatory information management, claims processing and adjudication, claims recovery and payment integrity, revenue cycle management, health equity analytics, and care services. Its High Tech and Manufacturing segment offers solutions for trust and safety, advertising sales support, customer and user experience, customer care support, supply chain management, direct and indirect procurement, logistics, field, aftermarket support, and engineering services. It offers digital operations, data-tech-AI, advisory, agent technology; and finance and accounting, human resources, sales and commercial operations, marketing, and global business solutions. The company has strategic alliance with Google Cloud. The company was founded in 1997 and is based in Hamilton, Bermuda.

Each employee generates $5K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $631 per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 59× revenue per employee (elevated relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: Genpact Limited is a mid-cap technology business with a $7.3B market cap on $5.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 8% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 37%.

The business throws off $735M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.47× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.4× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 10.2×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.6%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sector_headwinds.text: Low reinvestment-driven growth suggests the compounding engine has stalled
Fragmented industry with below-average profit capture — no moat to protect margins
Above-average short interest at 7.3% of float
Insiders are net sellers (100% sell ratio, net $11.1M) — the people closest to the business are reducing their personal stake
Technology sector lagging the market significantly, underperforming by 7% over 3 months
Elevated sector volatility (38% annualized) adds uncertainty
Antitrust and platform-regulation risk — the larger the network effect, the larger the regulatory target on its back, and a single consent decree can reset the moat.
AI disruption of existing software moats — incumbents with durable margins face commoditisation as AI-native competitors replicate features at a fraction of the R&D cost.
Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sector_tailwinds: Trading at a 57% margin of safety to estimated fair value — a real cushion against errors in the estimate
Market is pricing in lower growth than the company has historically delivered
Valued at a 45% discount to sector median EV/EBITDA
Healthy payout ratio leaves room for both dividend growth and reinvestment

sect: Its 15% operating margin runs 8pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.63x).
It accounts for 0.1% of sector revenue and 0.1% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-4.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 21% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 26% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 10% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 38% and a beta of 0.73, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.01 vs 5y 0.64), so read it loosely.
About $68.8M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 49% in the 2020 crash, 28% in the 2022 bear market and 60% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 57% below its DCF fair value of $101, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 24%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $80.68 to $132 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 12.7 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 9.2 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 9.9 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 27% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 10.1% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 9.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 11 covering analysts target $47.64 on average, 9% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 18% clears the cost of capital of 8.0% by 10pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.19).
It runs a 37% gross margin and converts 14% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.47x.
ROE of 22% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.3x equity multiplier).
It spends 1.8% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.4x net debt to EBITDA ($1.2B of cash against $1.5B of debt), with interest covered 10.2x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.2, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.1% over 3 years, 6.5% over 5 years and 7.5% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 7.4% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.02, a backlog worth 5% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 64%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 1.5% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 19, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.6%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (10 sales, net $11.1M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.6% (1.7% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 2.0% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 142,000 employees, each generates about $36K of revenue, 0.1x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 9.7% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $5K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.1M (59x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
